item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated chat): "Implement `retry_budget.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Repository: quality-retry-budget. Read SPEC.md first; it is the source of truth.

Spec summary (SPEC.md is authoritative; reproduce it exactly):
- Pure function retry_delay(attempt, elapsed_ms, *, max_attempts=4, budget_ms=1000, base_ms=100, cap_ms=400, retry_after_ms=None) -> int | None.
- All values integer ms. attempt = attempts already made (initial is 1); elapsed_ms = total elapsed at failure.
- No sleeping, no clock, no mutation of inputs, no randomness, no third-party packages.
1. Validate ALL arguments before any early return. Each number must be a built-in int (reject bool and float). attempt and max_attempts >= 1. elapsed_ms, budget_ms, base_ms, cap_ms, and retry_after_ms when not None >= 0. Invalid values raise ValueError. No upper bound. base_ms may exceed cap_ms.
2. If attempt >= max_attempts return None. attempt > max_attempts is legal.
3. backoff = min(cap_ms, base_ms * 2**(attempt - 1)). Zero base or zero cap yields zero backoff. Saturate without building a huge power of two (e.g. cap the exponent or stop once the product reaches cap_ms).
4. If retry_after_ms is given, delay = max(backoff, retry_after_ms); this floor is NOT limited by cap_ms.
5. Return None if elapsed_ms + delay >= budget_ms; otherwise return delay (zero allowed). Never shorten the wait.

Deliverables:
- retry_budget.py implementing the above, keeping the existing public name and signature.
- test_retry_budget.py: keep existing tests; add focused tests for every validation error (bool, float, negative, zero attempt/max_attempts, each argument), attempt boundary (== max, > max), budget boundary (exactly budget_ms returns None, one less returns delay), cap saturation, zero base/cap, huge attempt values (e.g. 10**6, no large allocation), base > cap, retry_after above cap, retry_after below backoff, retry_after pushing past budget.
- Standard library only (unittest or pytest-compatible unittest). Run the tests and confirm they pass.
- Keep functions under 60 lines; at least two meaningful assertions/validations per non-trivial function; no try/except that hides failures.
- Commit the work. Commit identity: use the repo's existing configured git user only; do not override it. Do not add any AI-generated or Claude attribution to the commit message. No questions to the operator; if the spec is genuinely ambiguous, follow the most literal reading and say so in the summary.

pr.body: Files: retry_budget.py (validation helpers, _backoff with shift clamp, retry_delay), test_retry_budget.py (existing 3 tests kept, 33 focused tests added). Validation runs before any early return and raises ValueError for non-int (bool/float included), out-of-range values. Backoff clamps the shift to cap_ms.bit_length() so huge attempts never build a large power of two. Retry-After is an uncapped floor. Budget boundary is strict (elapsed + delay >= budget returns None). Checks: unittest 36 OK; py_compile OK. Review: one reviewer, pass, no blocking findings. Non-blocking follow-up: test_huge_attempt_saturates_without_large_allocation checks the value only, not allocation; its name overstates this. Assumption: non-int types raise ValueError (spec says invalid values raise ValueError), not TypeError.
pr.summary: made retry_delay usable: validated, bounded retry scheduling per SPEC.md. now can compute retry waits with budget and attempt limits. before: stub raised NotImplementedError, now: 36 passing tests.
